plan.gentle: If I stay spread across too many classes, clubs, or roles, then I will ask which doors still serve my goals and release the rest.
plan.direct: If school commitments feel hard to drop simply because they are open, then I will separate identity loss from actual academic value.

front.competitive: How do backups keep charging the main road?

back.gentle: Because open options can divide attention and reduce progress on the path that matters most.
back.direct: Switching costs and fragmented focus weaken performance on the chosen path.

front.gentle: Why can closure feel more painful than the option is valuable?

front.competitive: Why do people keep doors alive that are barely paying?

back.direct: Threatened loss inflates weak alternatives and makes people overmaintain them.
back.competitive: They are pricing the sting of losing the door, not the payoff of the door.

keyTakeawayCard.gentle: The chapter teaches that preserving every option can quietly drain the path you actually value, so closure can be a tool for better freedom.
